q: 1. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient uphill side, involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: When the actual ground rises above (uphill of) the proposed contour gradient line, material must be excavated from the centre line to bring the road to the designed level.

q: 2. Two hill tops A and B 20 km apart are intervened by a third top C. If the top most contour of the three hill tops are of the same value, state whether the line of sight AB
options: passes below the hill top C
passes below the hill top C
explain: If all three hill tops have the same elevation, and C lies between A and B, the line of sight AB just touches (grazes) hill top C due to the curvature of the earth affecting the intermediate point differently.

q: 3. The best method of interpolation of contours, is by
explain: Graphical interpolation (using a series of parallel equally-spaced lines or a tracing paper method) is the most accurate and commonly preferred method of interpolating contour points.

q: 4. For preparation of contour plan for a route survey
options: method of trace contour is used
method of cross profile is used
indirect method of contouring is used
explain: For route surveys (roads, railways), contour plans are prepared using cross-sections taken perpendicular to the centre line, i.e., the method of cross profile.

q: 5. Accuracy of elevation of various points obtained from contour map is limited to
explain: The accuracy of elevations read from a contour map is generally limited to about half (1/2) of the contour interval, since contours are drawn at discrete intervals.

q: 6. The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours, is called
explain: The constant difference of elevation between two consecutive contour lines is termed the contour interval.

q: 7. The V-shaped contour represents
explain: Contours crossing a stream or depression form V-shapes pointing upstream (toward higher ground), representing a valley; a ridge would show contours pointing away from higher ground (downhill).

q: 8. The direction of steepest slope on the contour, is
options: at an angle of 45 deg to the contour
at right angles to the contour
explain: The steepest slope at any point on the ground is always along the line perpendicular (at right angles) to the contour at that point, since contours represent equal elevation.

q: 9. Two contour lines, having the same elevation
explain: Two contours of the same elevation can unite/merge together, for example in the case of a vertical cliff, where multiple contour lines coincide at a single line on the map.

q: 10. Closed contours of decreasing values towards their centre, represent
explain: When the innermost closed contour has the lowest elevation value, the feature represents a depression (a hollow); a hill is represented by closed contours of increasing value towards the centre.

q: 11. The angle of intersection of a contour and a ridge line, is
explain: A ridge line runs along the line of steepest ascent, and since contours are always perpendicular to the direction of steepest slope, a contour crosses a ridge (or valley) line at right angles (90 deg).

q: 12. In case of a double line river, contours are
options: stopped at the banks of the river
stopped at the edge of the river
drawn by parabolic curves having their vertex at the centre of the water
explain: For a river shown by double lines (its two banks), contour lines are stopped at the edge/bank of the river since the ground under water is not part of the mapped topographic surface.

q: 13. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called
explain: A line on the ground surface that maintains a constant inclination (gradient) to the horizontal throughout is called a contour gradient (grade contour), unlike a contour line which is horizontal (constant elevation).

q: 14. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient up hill side involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: When the actual road alignment on the uphill side deviates from (cuts across, rising faster than) the contour gradient, the road surface lies below the natural ground, requiring excavation along the centre line.

q: 15. Bergchund is a topographical feature in
explain: Bergchund/bergschrund-type terrain features are associated with hilly/mountainous topography, as per the book's classification.

q: 16. The relief representation on the map can be depicted
explain: Relief (terrain relief) on a map can be shown using multiple methods - spot levels, altitude tinting/layers, and hill shading - so all of the above apply.

q: 17. The suitable contour interval for a map with scale 1 : 10000 is
explain: For a relatively large scale map such as 1:10000, a fine contour interval of about 2 m is typically suitable to show ground detail adequately.

q: 18. Which of the following methods of contouring is most suitable for hilly terrain?
explain: The tacheometric method of contouring is most suitable for hilly terrain because it quickly provides both horizontal distance and elevation to numerous points without the need for chaining across difficult ground.

q: 19. A series of closely spaced contour lines represents a
explain: Closely spaced contour lines indicate a rapid change in elevation over a short horizontal distance, representing a steep slope.

q: 20. Direct method of contouring is
explain: The direct method of contouring, where points actually lying on the contour are located and marked in the field, is the most accurate method, though it is slower than indirect methods.

q: 21. The angle of intersection of a counter and a ridge line, is
explain: Contour lines always cross ridge or valley lines at right angles (90 degrees), since ridge/valley lines represent the direction of steepest slope, which is perpendicular to the contour.

q: 22. In case of double line river, contours are
options: stopped at the banks of the river
stopped at the edge of the river
drawn by parabolic curves having their vertex at the centre of the water
explain: For a double line (wide) river, contours are shown stopping at the edge/bank of the river rather than being drawn across the water body.

q: 23. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called
explain: A contour gradient is an imaginary line on the ground surface that maintains a constant inclination (slope) to the horizontal throughout its length.

q: 24. From any point on the surface with a given inclination
options: only one contour gradient is possible
explain: From any given point with a specified inclination, two contour gradients are geometrically possible - one running in each direction around the slope at that constant grade.

q: 25. Location of contour gradient for a highway is best set out from
explain: For highway alignment, the contour gradient is best set out starting from a saddle (low point on a ridge) and working down the hill, providing more efficient routing options.

q: 26. A contour map of the area is essential before proceeding with the construction of
explain: A detailed contour map is essential before constructing a dam, since it is critical for determining reservoir capacity, submergence area, and the layout of the dam and spillway.

q: 27. The contours merge or cross one another on the map in case of
explain: Contours merge (coincide) at a vertical cliff surface, and actually cross one another only in the special case of overhanging ground/caves, so all these listed conditions represent exceptions to the normal rule.

q: 28. Contour lines
explain: Contour lines are always continuous closed loops; they never end abruptly but must eventually close somewhere, either within the map area or by returning to the same elevation elsewhere.

q: 29. Contours are used to determine
options: indivisibility of points on a contour map
area of the drainage basin and capacity of the reservoir
explain: Contour maps are versatile tools used to determine intervisibility of points, drainage basin areas and reservoir capacities, and earthwork quantities, so all listed uses apply.

q: 30. Contour lines look to cross each other in case of
explain: Only in the special case of an overhanging cliff can contour lines appear to cross each other in plan view, since one part of the ground overhangs another at a different elevation but same horizontal projection.

q: 31. Closed contours with higher value inside represents a
explain: When the innermost closed contour has the highest elevation value, it represents a hill (elevated feature).

q: 32. The vertical distance between any two consecutive contours is called
explain: The constant vertical distance between any two consecutive contour lines on a map is, by definition, the contour interval.

q: 33. The horizontal distance between any two consecutive contours is called
explain: The horizontal distance between two consecutive contours (which varies with the slope) is called the horizontal equivalent.

q: 34. When several contours coincide, it indicates
explain: When multiple contour lines of different elevations coincide (appear as a single line) on a map, it indicates a vertical cliff, where elevation changes without any horizontal distance.

q: 35. The vertical distance between the elevations represented by adjacent contour lines on a map is called
explain: As defined before, the constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours on a map is the contour interval.

q: 36. An imaginary line on the surface of the earth having a constant inclination with the horizontal (slope) is called
explain: As defined earlier, an imaginary line on the ground maintaining a constant slope (inclination to horizontal) is called a contour gradient.

q: 37. Contour interval is
options: inversely proportional to the scale of the map
directly proportional to the flatness of ground
larger if the time available is more
explain: A larger map scale (more detailed) generally uses a smaller contour interval and vice versa, so the contour interval is inversely proportional to the scale of the map.

q: 38. In route surveys, the most suitable method of contouring is
explain: For a linear route survey (road, railway, canal), contouring by cross-sections taken perpendicular to the centre line at regular intervals is the most suitable method.

q: 39. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation of contours is
explain: Interpolating contour positions between spot levels by arithmetical (proportional) calculation is considered the most accurate method, though graphical and estimation methods are quicker alternatives.

q: 40. An imaginary line joining the points of equal elevation on the surface of the earth, represents
explain: By definition, a contour line is an imaginary line on the earth's surface joining points of equal elevation.

q: 41. The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours, is called
explain: The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours on a map is, by definition, the contour interval.

q: 42. The contour interval is kept inversely proportional to
options: time and expense of field work
steepness of the configuration of the area
explain: Contour interval selection is influenced by multiple inversely related factors together - available time/budget, steepness of terrain, and map scale - so all of the above apply.

q: 43. The representation of general topography of a very flat terrain is possible only
options: by drawing contours at large interval
by drawing contours at small interval
by giving spot levels at large interval
by giving spot levels to features at close interval
explain: For very flat terrain, contours (even at a small interval) would be too widely spaced or non-existent to show relief adequately, so spot levels given at close intervals to features are needed instead.

q: 44. Contour interval, within the limits of a map
options: may vary according to the configuration
explain: Within a single map, the contour interval must be kept constant throughout, so that the spacing of contours consistently reflects the actual ground slope.

q: 45. The direction of steepest slope on a contour, is
options: at an angle of 45 to the contour
at right angles to the contour
explain: The direction of steepest slope at any point on a contour is always perpendicular (at right angles) to that contour line.

q: 46. Straight, parallel and widely spaced contours represent
explain: Contours that are straight, parallel, and uniformly (widely) spaced indicate a uniformly sloping, inclined plane surface.

q: 47. Two contour lines, having the same may cross each other only in the case of
explain: Two contour lines of the same elevation can unite (coincide/merge) together in special cases such as at a vertical cliff, though they do not typically cross transversely.

q: 48. Contours of different elevations may cross each other only in the case of
explain: Only at an overhanging cliff can contours of different elevations appear to cross each other in plan, since the overhang causes two different elevations to project onto the same horizontal location.

q: 49. Closed contours of decreasing values toward their centre, represent
explain: When closed contour loops show decreasing elevation values toward the centre, they represent a depression (low point), as opposed to a hill where values increase toward the centre.

q: 50. Contour lines cross ridge or valley lines at
explain: Contour lines always cross ridge or valley lines at right angles (90 degrees), since these lines represent the direction of steepest slope, perpendicular to the contour.
